docs.title: Testing Earth Observation Application Packages
docs.text:
This repository provides a working example of testing an Earth Observation Application Package (EOAP) with Common Workflow Language (CWL). It combines a declarative test suite, satellite data fixtures, and expected outputs for a water-body detection application.

The processing application is supplied by the external app-water-bodies-cloud-native release, version 1.1.0. This repository contains its testing baseline rather than the processing implementation.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Getting started: prepare your environment and run a first test.
  • Water-bodies example: follow the processing stages and understand the six existing cases.
  • Writing tests: define inputs and assertions for your own application.
  • Fixtures and reproducibility: maintain datasets and review deterministic outputs.
  • Continuous integration: understand automation and preview this documentation.
  • Troubleshooting: diagnose execution and comparison failures.

docs.title: How the pieces fit together
docs.text:
cwltest reads the YAML test definitions and invokes a CWL runner, here cwltool. The runner executes the selected tool or workflow using its job inputs. The test framework then compares the returned outputs with the expectations in the suite. See the upstream cwltest project for the framework's command-line entry points.

flowchart LR Suite[Test suite] --> Test[cwltest] Inputs[Job inputs and fixtures] --> Runner[cwltool] Test --> Runner Package[CWL application package] --> Runner Runner --> Outputs[Actual outputs] Outputs --> Compare[Compare expectations] Suite --> Compare

docs.title: What passing tests establish
docs.text:
The suite exercises individual processing steps and their connection in a complete workflow. Fixed checksums provide evidence that selected artifacts match the baseline byte for byte. Flexible file assertions provide narrower evidence: a step returned the expected kind of output.

Passing this suite alone does not establish scientific accuracy, STAC schema compliance, performance, or successful deployment through an OGC API Processes service. Add dedicated checks for those properties when they are part of your application's requirements. Likewise, portability to another runner needs execution and validation on that runner.

docs.title: Repository map
docs.text:
tests/
  test-suite.yaml      # Cases and expected outputs
  inputs-01.yaml      # Green-band crop
  inputs-02.yaml      # Near-infrared crop
  inputs-03.yaml      # Normalized difference
  inputs-04.yaml      # Thresholding
  inputs-05.yaml      # Catalog generation
  inputs-e2e.yaml     # Full workflow
  data/               # Source and intermediate fixtures
docs/                 # This guide
mkdocs.yml            # Website configuration
.github/workflows/    # Tests and documentation automation

docs.title: Test automation
docs.text:
.github/workflows/run-tests.yaml executes the suite on pushes and pull requests. It checks out the repository, prepares Python 3.11 on Ubuntu, installs the test dependencies, and runs:

cwltest --test tests/test-suite.yaml --tool cwltool --verbose --

The dependency installation pins cwltest==2.6.20250818005349 and leaves cwltool unpinned. Use the same versions and invocation locally when investigating CI failures.

The existing workflow is the source of truth for this repository's CI configuration. When adapting it to another EOAP, update the suite path and ensure the runner has access to required containers and data.

docs.title: Make failures reviewable
docs.text:
Review the failed case's execution log before changing expected outputs. Distinguish dependency-download failures, application failures, and assertion mismatches.

If more diagnostics are needed, consider retaining generated artifacts and logs with a CI artifact-upload step. The current workflow does not include such a step. Keep retained data small and avoid including credentials or private input data.

Changes to remote fixtures can affect all cases consuming those URLs, even when their YAML files are unchanged. Include fixture changes in regression review and use the baseline review process.

docs.title: Preview this guide
docs.text:
From the repository root, with your Python environment active:

python -m pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin
mkdocs serve

Open the local URL printed by MkDocs. Navigation is configured in mkdocs.yml; page content is stored under docs/.

Build the static site without deploying it:

mkdocs build --strict

Strict mode treats warnings as build failures, helping catch broken documentation references before publication.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
.github/workflows/docs.yaml builds and publishes the site with mkdocs gh-deploy --force. It runs on pushes to main or develop when changes affect docs/**, mkdocs.yml, or .github/**.

Both configured branches can trigger publication. Review branch and path filters when changing the release process. Local mkdocs serve and mkdocs build preview or build the site without publishing it.

docs.title: Maintain the guide
docs.text: Add new pages to the navigation, use relative links between documentation pages, and keep examples aligned with the checked-in suite. Verify commands and assertions when changing dependency versions or the referenced CWL release.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Use Python 3.11 to match this repository's CI environment. Have Docker installed and running for execution of containerised application steps. You also need network access to retrieve the CWL release, referenced input URLs, and container images.

Clone the repository and enter its root directory:

git clone https://github.com/eoap/testing-framework.git
cd testing-framework

docs.title: Install the test tools
docs.text:
Create an isolated Python environment:

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install cwltest==2.6.20250818005349 cwltool

On Windows, activate the environment with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell instead of the source command.

The cwltest pin matches the checked-in CI workflow. cwltool is currently unpinned, so separate installations can select different runner versions.

Check that the tools and container daemon are available:

cwltest --help
cwltool --version
docker info

docs.title: Run one case
docs.text:
Start with the catalog-generation case, which uses an existing mask fixture:

cwltest --test tests/test-suite.yaml --id stac-generation

This still retrieves the remote application definition and referenced STAC item. It is not an offline test.

docs.title: Run the complete suite
docs.text:
Use the same command as CI:

cwltest --test tests/test-suite.yaml --tool cwltool --verbose --

Read both execution logs and output-comparison messages. An execution failure means the runner could not complete the application; a comparison failure means its returned result did not match the test expectation. See troubleshooting for the next checks.

docs.title: Understand input resolution
docs.text:
The suite refers to jobs such as inputs-03.yaml beside test-suite.yaml. File inputs within those jobs refer to fixtures such as data/crop_green.tif. Keep this directory relationship when moving or copying tests.

Some inputs are URL strings rather than CWL File objects. The application interprets those strings as STAC item references. Replacing one with a local file requires checking the corresponding CWL input type and the application's handling of that value.

Continue with the water-bodies example to understand what each case executes.

docs.title: Fixtures and reproducibility
docs.text: A reproducible test needs a known application, known input data, and a stable execution environment. Fixed expected outputs help detect changes, but they do not freeze those dependencies by themselves.

docs.title: Current baseline
docs.text:
Dependency Repository behavior Consequence CWL application Release URL for version 1.1.0 Cases select a specific application release cwltest CI pins 2.6.20250818005349 Local setup can match the framework version cwltool Unpinned in CI Runner behavior may change between installations Remote fixtures URLs reference main Data may change without changing the CWL release Containers Declared by the external CWL package Review that package's image references when diagnosing drift

For a stronger baseline, consider commit-based fixture URLs, an explicit runner version, and container image digests. Apply those changes deliberately to the application and suite, then validate the complete workflow.

docs.title: Fixture roles
docs.text:
tests/data/ contains source band rasters, a STAC item describing their assets, cropped band rasters, normalized-difference output, a thresholded mask, and catalog artifacts. Intermediate fixtures let unit cases run without recomputing every preceding stage.

Document the origin, acquisition date, area of interest, processing parameters, and redistribution terms when adding data. Retain the pixels and metadata needed to exercise the behavior while keeping fixtures small enough for routine CI execution.

A local edit to tests/data/item.json will not affect jobs that still read its URL on main. When experimenting with new fixtures, explicitly point inputs to the intended data source and check any asset URLs embedded in the item.

docs.title: Record expected bytes
docs.text:
On Linux, calculate a checksum and byte count for an inspected output:

sha1sum catalog.json
wc -c < catalog.json

Record the values in the expected output:

checksum: "sha1$<digest>"
size: 363

The digest placeholder must be replaced with the actual value. The size above illustrates the current catalog baseline; use the measured size for a new artifact.

For a collection of output files:

find output-directory -type f -exec sha1sum {} \;

Run these commands against generated artifacts whose contents you have reviewed. A checksum establishes equality to a chosen baseline, not correctness of that baseline.

docs.title: Review a baseline change
docs.text:
When a size or checksum changes, inspect the artifact before editing the expectation. JSON whitespace, field ordering, timestamps, raster compression, metadata, and actual pixel changes can all affect bytes.

  1. Identify whether the application, input data, runner, or container changed.
  2. Compare metadata and raster properties with the previous artifacts.
  3. Confirm the change meets the intended application behavior.
  4. Update all affected expectations. The catalog and end-to-end cases share the same three artifact expectations.
  5. Run the affected unit cases and the full workflow.
  6. Record why the new baseline is accepted in the pull request.

docs.title: Beyond byte equality
docs.text: For scientific validation, consider known reference masks, tolerances for floating-point rasters, nodata behavior, and coverage of different scene conditions. For STAC validation, add explicit schema and asset-link checks. These checks complement the current suite and require their own validation implementation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with the first failing case rather than the final suite summary. Run it independently with detailed output:

cwltest --test tests/test-suite.yaml --id crop-green --tool cwltool --verbose --

Replace crop-green with the failing test ID.

docs.title: Tools cannot be found
docs.text:
Activate the virtual environment used for installation, then check:

python -m pip show cwltest cwltool
cwltest --help
cwltool --version

If installation and execution use different environments, reinstall the tools in the active environment using the getting-started commands.

docs.title: Container startup fails
docs.text:
Check docker info in the same environment that launches the tests. Inspect the log for daemon connectivity, permission, image-download, or platform errors. Confirm that the application's container image can be accessed from the runner.

A successful Python dependency installation does not establish that containers can execute.

docs.title: Remote CWL or data cannot be retrieved
docs.text:
Identify the exact failed URL in the log. Check network access, proxy settings, release availability, and whether the referenced path exists.

The suite fetches the application from a release URL. Crop, catalog, and workflow inputs reference a STAC item on main, whose assets also point to remote rasters. Changing a local fixture does not automatically change those remote references.

docs.title: A local input file is missing
docs.text:
Check the job's location values and preserve the relationship between the suite, job YAML, and data/ directory. For example, inputs-03.yaml references data/crop_green.tif and data/crop_nir.tif beside the job's directory.

Confirm the files are present in your checkout before investigating application code.

docs.title: Input validation fails
docs.text:
Compare the job with the selected CWL process. Common causes include a misspelled input name, a scalar supplied where an array is expected, a URL string supplied where a File is expected, or selection of the wrong process fragment.

The crop cases select #crop; the full workflow selects #water-bodies. Their input names and output ports differ.

docs.title: Execution succeeds but comparison fails
docs.text:
Read which output field differs. A wrong output name or class suggests a changed interface. A size or checksum mismatch suggests changed artifact bytes.

The catalog-generation and end-to-end cases check the catalog, item, and mask. Follow the baseline review process before replacing expected hashes. Check whether the same mismatch occurs in both cases: shared failures can point to catalog serialization, fixtures, or a common environment dependency.

If unit cases pass and the full workflow fails, examine the connections between steps and the differences between saved intermediate fixtures and newly generated outputs.

docs.title: Local results differ from CI
docs.text:
Compare Python, cwltest, cwltool, container runtime, application release, and fixture references. CI currently pins only the test framework among the Python test dependencies.

Record the environment and the first meaningful error when reporting a failure. Include the test ID, command, relevant log excerpt, and whether the issue reproduces with a single case.

docs.title: The documentation build fails
docs.text:
Install mkdocs-material and mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin in the active environment. Run mkdocs build --strict from the repository root and inspect the first warning or error.

For a new page, check its navigation path in mkdocs.yml, relative links, and fenced code blocks. A missing Python package is an environment issue; a missing referenced page or asset requires correcting the documentation or site configuration.

docs.title: Water-bodies example
docs.text:
The test suite selects tools and the workflow from this release document:

https://github.com/eoap/mastering-app-package/releases/download/1.1.0/app-water-bodies-cloud-native.1.1.0.cwl

A fragment such as #crop selects a process in that CWL document. The end-to-end case selects #water-bodies.

docs.title: Processing stages
docs.text:
flowchart TD Item[STAC item] --> Green[Crop green band] Item --> NIR[Crop near-infrared band] Green --> NDWI[Normalized difference] NIR --> NDWI NDWI --> Otsu[Otsu thresholding] Otsu --> STAC[STAC catalog and water mask] Item --> STAC

The crop jobs use the bounding box -121.409,39.824,-120.73,40.482 and the coordinate reference system EPSG:4326. Their band parameter selects green or nir. The item fixture identifies a Sentinel-2B scene acquired on 13 July 2021 and provides asset links for those inputs.

Normalized difference combines the two cropped rasters into NDWI. Otsu thresholding converts that intermediate raster into a binary mask. The final step associates the mask with item metadata and writes a STAC catalog.

docs.title: Existing cases
docs.text:
ID CWL fragment Job Output assertion crop-green #crop inputs-01.yaml cropped: File, flexible location crop-nir #crop inputs-02.yaml cropped: File, flexible location normalized-difference #norm_diff inputs-03.yaml ndwi: File, flexible location otsu-threshold #otsu inputs-04.yaml binary_mask_item: File, flexible location stac-generation #stac inputs-05.yaml stac_catalog: Directory with sizes and checksums workflow-end-to-end #water-bodies inputs-e2e.yaml The same deterministic catalog expectation

The five unit cases execute application steps through the CWL runner. They can still require containers and network access. The normalized-difference, thresholding, and catalog cases use saved intermediate rasters, allowing each step to be investigated independently of upstream execution.

docs.title: End-to-end inputs
docs.text:
The full workflow uses this job structure:

stac_items:
  - https://github.com/eoap/testing-framework/raw/refs/heads/main/tests/data/item.json
aoi: "-121.409,39.824,-120.73,40.482"
epsg: "EPSG:4326"
bands:
  - green
  - nir

docs.title: Expected catalog
docs.text:
Both catalog tests check three files, including the water-mask raster:

catalog.json
S2B_10TFK_20210713_0_L2A/
  S2B_10TFK_20210713_0_L2A.json
  otsu.tif

The expected sizes in the suite are 363 bytes for the catalog, 2,755 bytes for the item, and 6,918 bytes for the mask. The suite also records a SHA-1 checksum for each file.

These comparisons detect changes to the baseline artifacts. They do not independently validate the STAC schemas or judge whether the detected water bodies are scientifically correct. See writing tests for choosing assertions and reproducibility for maintaining the baseline.

docs.title: Choose a test boundary
docs.text:
Use a tool-level case to isolate one processing stage and a workflow-level case to exercise the connections between stages. Saved intermediate fixtures make it easier to identify which stage introduced a regression.

Choose cases from the application's requirements: a representative scene, an area with no water, nodata at the crop boundary, or invalid parameters may warrant separate coverage. These are possible additions; the current suite contains only the six cases described in the example.

docs.title: Define a case
docs.text:
The suite is a YAML list. This complete case follows the existing crop test:

- id: crop-green
  doc: "Crop the green band for the example area of interest."
  tool: https://github.com/eoap/mastering-app-package/releases/download/1.1.0/app-water-bodies-cloud-native.1.1.0.cwl#crop
  job: inputs-01.yaml
  output:
    cropped:
      class: File
      location: Any
Field Purpose id Unique name used to select the case doc Description of the behavior being tested tool CWL document, optionally with a process fragment job YAML job containing the application's input values output Expected values keyed by CWL output names

Use descriptive IDs such as crop-green or workflow-end-to-end. Output names must match the selected CWL process; cropped and ndwi are different output ports.

docs.title: Supply job inputs
docs.text:
This is the normalized-difference job used by the repository:

rasters:
  - class: File
    location: data/crop_green.tif
  - class: File
    location: data/crop_nir.tif

Preserve array order when it affects the computation. Check the tool's declared input types before choosing a scalar, array, URL string, or CWL File object. The CWL input guide describes the input type system.

docs.title: Match assertion strength to the requirement
Flexible file outputs
docs.text:
output:
  ndwi:
    class: File
    location: Any

This avoids tying the expectation to an execution-specific path. It does not specify file contents, pixel values, or a checksum. Use it when successful execution and the output type are the intended checks, and add stronger validation when content matters.

docs.title: Deterministic files
docs.text:
The following excerpt uses the catalog baseline from the existing suite:

output:
  stac_catalog:
    class: Directory
    listing:
      - class: File
        location: catalog.json
        checksum: "sha1$70e96cddbb205363b4ee9cb763e438a29fd29cdc"
        size: 363

This excerpt covers only the top-level catalog. The repository's actual catalog tests also assert the nested item and raster. Model nested outputs with directory listings, following tests/test-suite.yaml.

Byte comparisons are useful when serialization and raster encoding are stable. If acceptable results can differ in encoding or numerical precision, consider a separate validation step that checks meaningful properties such as raster dimensions, CRS, nodata handling, class values, or numerical tolerance. Such semantic checks are not implemented by the current suite.

docs.title: Expected failures
docs.text: cwltest supports expected-failure cases through should_fail. Consult the upstream framework and the installed version's documentation before adding them. Design the input so the failure represents the intended invalid condition; a missing container or unavailable URL should not be mistaken for successful validation of application error handling.

docs.title: Add a case safely
docs.text:
1. Inspect the selected CWL process and its input/output names.
  2. Add a small, documented fixture and a job file under tests/.
  3. Add a uniquely named entry to tests/test-suite.yaml.
  4. Run the case with --id, inspect its artifacts, and establish expectations.
  5. Run the full suite to check for regressions.
  6. Explain any fixture or expected-output changes in the pull request.

See fixtures and reproducibility before updating checksums.
